remarks: Issued from Kaḷakkuḍi. States that while king Varaguṇa, son of Śrīmāra-Śrīvallabha, who was devoted to god Śiva, was ruling, two villages, Tirumaṅgalam and Śomāśikuṟichchi clubbed together into one were granted by the king (Parān-takaṉ-Vīranārāyaṇaṉ) to several Brāhmaṇas at the instance of Nārāyaṇaṉ-Kēśavaṉ, a learned Brāhmaṇa of Tirumaṅgalam. remarks: Records the sale of the village Taṭṭāṉkuḍikkāḍu alias Maṟu-māṇikkanallūr, a dēvadāna, to Mudaliyār Nāchchiyār, daughter of Vattarāyar of Amaṇpudukkuḷam in Karuṅguḍi-nāḍu by the Ūravar of Vēlaṅguḍi and the investment of the money amounting to 120 irāśi-paṇam thus realised as capital for the expenses of conducting a procession of the goddess Nāchchiyār around the temple.
